candidate_sentences.text: Consolidated revenue from contracts with customers declined by 3.6% to 200.9 million euros compared with 208.3 million euros in 2023.

Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes the goodwill impairment, stood at a negative 449 thousand euros.
Consequently, the group incurred a net loss of 7.6 million euros for 2024, compared with a net profit of 3.4 million euros reported in 2023.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key period-over-period changes included an 8% decline in served travelers (239 thousand in 2024 vs 259 thousand in 2023) and a swing from positive to negative EBITDA (€5.2m to -€6.1m). The result was primarily driven by increased competitive pressures in the Baltic travel market, particularly in Turkey and Greek islands, coupled with a one-off EUR 5.7 million goodwill impairment related to the Estonian cash-generating unit.

candidate_sentences.text: Novaturas AB reported weaker financial results for the year ended December 31, 2024, driven by an increased competitive environment, oversupply of travel options in the Baltic States, and intense price competition in key destinations such as Turkey and the Greek islands.
The total number of travelers served by the group decreased by 7.6% to 239 thousand passengers.

Operating expenses reached 27.5 million euros, representing a 25% increase from the previous year, primarily due to a one-off, non-cash goodwill impairment loss of 5.7 million euros identified in the Estonian cash-generating unit.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization dropped significantly to a negative 6.1 million euros from a positive 5.2 million euros in 2023.

verified_key_information_units.information: In early 2025, strategic investor Neset Kockar acquired 23.2% of Novaturas' shares (completed on 30 April 2025), with a planned further acquisition to reach 33.19% by autumn 2025. Kockar, a Turkish tourism businessman, provided the Group with loan facilities totaling EUR 2 million post-reporting-period, and is expected to bring synergies in destinations popular with Baltic travelers, potentially expanding hotel and travel offerings.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO’s Foreword; Note 29 (Events after the reporting period)

candidate_sentences.text: To strengthen its capital structure and market position, the company engaged in strategic alternative reviews and entered into transactions with a new strategic investor, Neset Kockar, who acquired a 23.2 percent equity stake in early 2025, with further ownership increases planned.
Additionally, the company secured supplementary credit lines and loan facilities from financial partners and the new investor to support ongoing operations and liquidity requirements moving forward.

verified_key_information_units.information: Travel demand trends showed significant growth to Spain (149% increase in passengers to Malaga, Barcelona, and Mallorca compared to 2022) and an 8% rise in long-haul travel. Popular long-haul destinations included Vietnam (+367%), Phuket (+23%), and Zanzibar (+21%), with long-haul flights achieving a 98.9% load factor in Q4 2024.

Operational performance improved materially in Q4 2024, with adjusted EBITDA reaching EUR 2.3 million and a load factor of 98.9% (compared to 96.7% in Q4 2023). This improvement followed optimization of the travel program and better destination management, reducing the share of last-minute trips which negatively impact financial results.

candidate_sentences.text: Despite the weaker overall annual performance, the company’s operating results demonstrated a material improvement starting in September 2024 following effective optimization of its travel program and reduction of unprofitable last-minute sales.
This optimization allowed the group to achieve a high seat capacity utilization load factor of 98.9% in the fourth quarter and operate profitably during that period.

verified_key_information_units.information: Liquidity position weakened with cash and cash equivalents decreasing to EUR 394 thousand at 31 December 2024 from EUR 3,347 thousand in 2023. Borrowings increased to EUR 9,250 thousand (from EUR 8,682 thousand in 2023), and the Group did not comply with all financial covenants as of year-end, requiring waivers from lenders.
